title: The normalized restriction comparison composes on chosen lattices
statement: For D,l,Ω and any supplied normalized realization R, completed system S, scalar-realization family A and RestrictionComparison C [def-zl-classical-lisse-restriction-models; def-zl-classical-lisse-restriction-maps], let T be a separated finite-type geometric base, M a common-stage heart object and P its supplied partition with lattices. Then SuccessiveRestrictions [def-zl-classical-frontier-restriction-data] holds: for every original stratum and two successive locally closed immersions h and a into it, C.iso for a≫h equals the composite built from the inverse of the actual raw restriction compositor, C.iso for a, pullback of C.iso for h and the inverse of the actual derived compositor. No frontier, finite-field model or Weil structure is asserted.

source.place: Paragraphs 6-7; normalized classical restriction, descent of the finite frontier and its actual Weil structures.

proof.text: Let $i:T_\nu\to T$ and let $h:W\to T_\nu$ be any of the locally closed factorizations in the statement. Write $N=(N_n)$ for its supplied lisse $\mathcal O_E$-lattice, so its reductions are finite locally free. The pulled-back system $(h^*N_n)_n$ is still a lattice system: pull back a finite-level trivializing etale cover and its basis, and pull back the transition isomorphism $N_{n+1}\otimes A_{E,n}\cong N_n$. Thus lisseness, finite freeness and that transition equation hold on the pulled-back cover. Apply the normalized classical-system realization on $W$. Its restriction comparison identifies this system's inverse limit followed by rationalization with $Lh^*Li^*M$, hence with $L(ih)^*M$ through the specified composition map of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. The comparison is natural in maps, commutes with finite coefficient extension, and satisfies composition, so for a further restriction $a:W'\to W$ its composite is precisely the comparison for $ha$. This proves the restriction and successive-restriction assertions without any Weil structure.
